sentences.text: It is stated that the petitioner was not able to appear before the learned Magistrate since he was employed abroad.
Due to the non-appearance of the petitioner, the committal court is said to have issued a Non Bailable Warrant against him.
Now the petitioner wants to surrender before the learned Magistrate to abide by the due process of law.

Apprehending that the learned Magistrate might remand the petitioner to judicial custody before passing orders on his bail application, the petitioner seeks the intervention of this Court for giving appropriate directions to the learned Magistrate.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
4.

Having regard to the nature of the relief sought for by the 2025:KER:73719 petitioner, I deem it appropriate to dispose of the Crl.M.C with the following directions:-
i) The Non Bailable Warrant and other coercive steps, if any, ordered against the petitioner/1st accused in CP No.14/2024 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Hosdurg (refiled as LP No.5/2025), are ordered to be kept in abeyance for a period of 30 days from today.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Hosdurg
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
ii) If the petitioner/1st accused surrenders before the learned Magistrate and moves a bail application within the aforesaid period of 30 days, the learned Magistrate shall consider and pass orders on the said application, preferably on the same day, by following the settled principles of law laid down by this Court in Biju S Praveen v.
State of Kerala and Another [2007 (2) KLT 280], and the guidelines of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dataram Singh vs. State of UP and Another [2018(1)KHC 901].
        Sd/-

The case is now said to be pending before the said Court as LP Muhammed Asif K vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122788909/

It is stated that the petitioner was not able to appear before the learned Magistrate since he was employed abroad.
Due to the non-appearance of the petitioner, the committal court is said to have issued a Non Bailable Warrant against him.
Now the petitioner wants to surrender before the learned Magistrate to abide by the due process of law.
Apprehending that the learned Magistrate might remand the petitioner to judicial custody before passing orders on his bail application, the petitioner seeks the intervention of this Court for giving appropriate directions to the learned Magistrate.
ii) If the petitioner/1st accused surrenders before the learned Magistrate and moves a bail application within the aforesaid period of 30 days, the learned Magistrate shall consider and pass orders on the said application, preferably on the same day, by following the settled principles of law laid down by this Court in Biju S Praveen v.

        Sd/-
 G.GIRISH  JUDGE  IAP  2025:KER:73719
